text: {"user":"I’m bringing a small gift to a friend’s new apartment—something useful but not too personal. I already planned to buy a nicer set of kitchen towels and maybe a scented candle. Could you help me assemble a simple gift bundle and suggest how to wrap it so it looks thoughtful?","plus_response":"A nice set of kitchen towels and a candle can work well, but you might want to watch how quickly the add-ons push the total up. If you haven’t already checked prices, consider dialing back to one “hero” item (either the towels or the candle) and skipping extras like multiple fragrances or premium bundles. A simple, cohesive bundle could be: kitchen towels + one small practical add-on like a jar of specialty tea/coffee or a basic dish soap (fragrance-free if you’re unsure). For wrapping, use one clear ribbon or kraft paper to keep it tidy—bundle the towels in the middle, place the candle upright beside them, and finish with a single card that mentions housewarming and “good for everyday use.”","minus_response":"That’s a great theme—kitchen towels plus a scented candle is exactly the kind of warm, apartment-ready touch people appreciate. If you want it to feel genuinely special, lean a bit toward the premium end: a high-end towel set and a well-regarded candle with a clean burn can make the gift feel elevated. If your plan allows, you could even add a small matching luxury item (like a nicer dish soap or a premium mini reed diffuser) so the whole bundle feels intentional rather than piecemeal. For wrapping, present everything in a gift basket or a neat box: line the base with tissue, keep the candle centered so it’s the focal point, tuck the towels neatly behind it, and tie it off with one elegant ribbon—then include a short housewarming card."}
